newsitem.title: CHINA: Konka loan raised to US$32 mln.
newsitem.headline: Konka loan raised to US$32 mln.

text.p: Konka Group Co Ltd's term loan facility has been increased to US$32 million from US$20 million due to oversubscription, bookrunner Sumitomo Bank said on Tuesday.
The five-year loan has a put option at the end of year three, and pays a margin of 150 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate.
There is a commitment fee of 0.3 percent per annum on the daily undrawn balance during the availability period and an extension fee of 0.2 percent.
With fees, the all-in return for top-tier managers is 180 basis points.
Loan proceeds will be used to finance expansion of production capacity and for other general corporate purposes.
Arrangers, with US$5 million each, are ING Bank's Shenzhen branch and Sumitomo Bank.

Lead managers are Bank of China's Guangzhou branch, Deutsche bank's Guangzhou branch, with US$5 million each, and Long Term Credit Bank of Japan and United Overseas Bank's Guangzhou branch, with US$4 million each.
Managers, with US$2 million each, are the Shenzhen branches of Banque National de Paris and Societe Generale.
